localBiteReport: Redfish are the standout inshore species on Choctawhatchee Bay right now, with the bite remaining productive on the flats despite water clarity disrupted by Hurricane Isaias's October 9 landfall near Destin. Capt. Blake Nelson (Last Cast Charters) reports that smaller slot-sized reds — roughly 23 inches and under — are still holding in familiar guts, potholes, and shallow feeding areas, with cut mullet on Carolina rigs out-fishing live bait in some sessions. Speckled trout are also showing for anglers who can locate bait concentrations, with fish in the 22–27-inch range reported around the Destin area as of late October, though trout remain somewhat scattered between their summer and winter patterns due to the mixed weather. Redfish are also congregating around the bridges, jetties, and East Pass on incoming tides, and the captainexperiences.com guide network reports the overall bay bite heating up in conjunction with the Destin Fishing Rodeo this month. Water temperature at time of report: 75°F.
